proposals.break: At the FY2026 annual report on **1 April 2027**, net sales below **CHF410m** or EBITDA margin below **19.0%** would disprove the claim that signed backlog was merely shifting revenue while preserving economics; either outcome puts the position under §5.1. Also break if the company reports material cancellations or credit losses in the CHF357.9m H1 backlog, because that would invalidate the evidence this thesis uses for future demand ([company calendar and H1 update](https://ir.the-rsgroup.com/news/rands-group-provides-trading-update-for-h1-2026/bb41967c-ac88-4041-be50-200b3f26951b)).

proposals.warning: In the Q3 FY2027 filing scheduled for **17 November 2026**, trigger a full re-read if quarter-end receivable days exceed **65 days** (`accounts receivable ÷ quarterly revenue × 91`, versus 59.6 days now), or if any disclosed customer-support category—equity investments and commitments, AI-cloud agreements and third-party leases, or guarantees—grows by more than **20%** while Data Center revenue grows more slowly. This is the earliest disclosed evidence that credit and support may be pulling demand forward; it is not an automatic sale ([Q2 filing](https://investor.nvidia.com/files/doc_financials/2027/NVDA-2027-Q2-10Q-Final-including-exhibits.pdf), [local result date](../../prices.json)).
proposals.break: By the FY2027 annual filing, checkable on **1 March 2027**, the position should go under §5.1 if NVIDIA reports a material customer or partner default, a called guarantee, or a credit-loss provision tied to these support arrangements; it also breaks if receivable days remain above 65 for two consecutive quarters **and** a support category continues growing faster than Data Center revenue in both. That combination would show that reported growth is increasingly dependent on NVIDIA's balance sheet rather than customers' cash-backed demand ([Q2 filing](https://investor.nvidia.com/files/doc_financials/2027/NVDA-2027-Q2-10Q-Final-including-exhibits.pdf)). The company does not disclose how much revenue comes from customers it invests in, finances or guarantees, so the central circular-demand risk is **not fully falsifiable today**. The reduced £75 size, rather than the £125 maximum, is the cost of that missing disclosure.
